title: nightshift-surge-signal-dissect-and-rapid-runbook
body:
Summary:
During a late-evening traffic spike (approx 22:10 UTC) a subset of Dedicated GPU pools began reporting large latency outliers and progressive request queuing. Impact was primarily on customers with long-context generation jobs pinned to these pools; hosted API traffic routed to other model variants saw mild latency increase but no errors. Total customer-facing errors: 0; SLA latency SLO breaches: intermittent on 3 tenants for ~45 minutes.

Why this doc exists:
This is a capture of on-call observations, a working hypothesis tree, and an actionable rapid runbook draft for future similar events. The goal is to be prescriptive for night crews and to surface longer-term fixes for engineering. Treat as iterative; comments welcome.

Detection / Signal:
- Primary alert: pool-p99-latency > 4x baseline for a Dedicated-GPU pool (alert id: SRE-pool-latency-7).
- Secondary signals: allocator-throttle-rate increased in prometheus (allocator_throttle_total), eviction rate spike, and KV-cache hit ratio drop for several model variants.
- Correlated spike in 'long-running-batches' metric from inference runtime.

Initial timeline (UTC):
- 22:08: automated escalation triggered when p99 exceeded 4x.
- 22:10: oncall paged; viewable via alert payload and the pool dashboard.
- 22:12: confirmed many queued requests in flight recorder for pool 'dedicated-prod-us-west-3-a'.
- 22:18: preliminary mitigation: increased allocator concurrency cap on the pool (temporary knob).
- 22:22: observed eviction storm on ephemeral guests; some tenants moved to fallback pool.
- 22:31: autoscale controller attempted to add nodes; node launch succeeded but placement delayed ~6 minutes.
body_continued:
Metrics observed (selected):
- p50/p95/p99 baseline pre-incident: 13ms / 60ms / 180ms. Incident p99 peaked ~1.2s.
- allocator_throttle_total: baseline 0.1/min -> peaked 45/min.
- evictions/min: baseline 0.2 -> peaked 12.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: dropped from 0.82 -> 0.46 for model xlnet-embedder-v3 on that pool.
- sustained queue length: 0 -> ~320 requests backlogged around 22:10.

Immediate mitigations attempted (what we did):
1) Scoped routing change: shifted best-effort customers off the affected pool to dedicated-prod-us-west-3-b to reduce pressure. (22:14)
2) Allocator concurrency cap increased from 96 -> 128 for the pool (22:18). This reduced tail latency slightly but increased eviction activity.
3) Temporary autoscale loosen: reduced cooldowns so controller could add capacity faster (22:20). New capacity healthy around 22:28 but placement lagged.
4) Fine-grained eviction pause for tenants with pinned long sessions (experimental knob) to prevent thrashing; rolled back after 9 minutes due to resource oversubscription (22:29 - 22:38).

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
- Hypothesis A (most likely): Long tail of large-token generation jobs (few tenants) combined with continuous batching expansion caused per-GPU memory LRU pressure and KV-cache churn. This amplified allocator throttling and triggered eviction cascade. Evidence: spike in long-running-batches metric, lowered kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Hypothesis B: Miscalibrated autoscale cooldowns (recent change in PR #867) delayed capacity addition causing transient overload. Evidence: controller activity logs show queued scaling requests; PR #867 introduced a 60s cooldown increase.
- Hypothesis C: Noisy-tenant behavior from a single customer running many concurrent short-but-high-concurrency jobs (opportunistic burst) causing contention. Evidence weaker: tenant-level request histograms show a few high concurrency sessions but not sufficient alone to explain pool-wide KV drop.

Why this event was different from previous incidents:
- Cache amplification (kv cache miss cascade) played a larger role than raw GPU utilization; previous incidents were often pure allocation CPU/GPU saturations.
- Autoscale config change (PR #867) was in prod for two days leading to a narrower window where controller reaction was degraded.

Rapid runbook (for on-call) - Triage + stopgap actions (ordered):
Step 0: Pager response and communications
- Ack the alert, post to ops-oncall Slack channel with pool and p99 numbers.
- Notify Solutions Eng for any impacted enterprise customers.

Step 1: Quickly assess scope (5 minutes)
- Command: open pool dashboard (link in alert) — check p99, queue length, evictions/min, kv_cache_hit_rate.
- If queue length > 200 and p99 > 4x baseline -> proceed to Step 2.

Step 2: Throttle noisy sources (5-15 minutes)
- Use tenant-isolate script to reduce concurrency for tenants showing > 20 concurrent connections (commands and ACLs documented in internal repo).
- If tenant cannot be identified quickly, perform coarse route-shift of best-effort traffic to sibling pool (route service: /admin/route-shift).

Step 3: Adjust allocator knobs (experimental, do cautiously)
- Increase allocator concurrency cap by +25% for the affected pool, monitor evictions/min.
- If evictions > 8/min after increase, revert immediately.

Step 4: Autoscale controller adjustments (if capacity lagging)
- Temporarily bypass cooldowns for the controller for this pool (change via /admin/autoscale-overrides) to let scaling proceed.
- If new nodes are still not placed within 5 minutes, open infra ticket to check provisioning logs for cloud provider throttling.

Step 5: Eviction policy fallbacks
- If eviction cascade observed (evictions/min > 10), enable emergency-eviction-guard (prevents eviction of pinned tenants for 10 minutes) to avoid thrash. Use with caution: this can lead to overload if misused.

Step 6: Post-stabilization steps (after p99 returns to baseline for 10 minutes)
- Revert any temporary knobs (allocator caps, autoscale bypass).
- Collect data: export recorder trace for the period, snapshots of kv cache heatmap and tenant request traces. Attach to incident ticket.

Checklist for night crews (quick cheat-sheet):
- key dashboards: pool-health, allocator-metrics, kv-cache-heatmap, autoscale-controller.
- critical metrics to watch: p99, queue length, evictions/min, allocator_throttle_total, kv_cache_hit_rate.
- contact list: infra-oncall, solutions-eng, release-eng if PRs were rolled out within 48h.

Longer-term remediation recommendations (engineering work items):
1) Revert or re-evaluate PR #867 autoscale cooldown change; add staged rollout and feature flag for cooldowns. (owner: release-eng)
2) Implement KV cache backpressure signal to allocator so cache churn can throttle batching growth before allocator throttles. (owner: serving-runtime)
3) Improve tenant-level telemetry to detect noisy patterns earlier (tenant concurrency per-second, large-token-run counters). (owner: observability)
4) Hardening autoscale placement: add placement timeouts and faster fallbacks to sibling pools when placement delayed > 90s. (owner: infra)
5) Formalize emergency knobs and testing matrix so oncall knows safe bounds and automated reverts. (owner: eng-sre)

Open action items (owners + due dates):
- Evan Chen: Draft PR to add feature flag for autoscale cooldown rollback (due 2025-11-20).
- Marisol Vega: Instrument tenant concurrency exporter and onboarding plan for a/b testing (due 2025-12-05).
- Jonas Meyer: Run chaotic load test for KV cache churn scenarios on staging to validate backpressure heuristics (due 2025-11-30).
- Aisha Raman: Update this runbook with exact admin commands and add to SRE runbook index (due 2025-11-12).

Post-incident review notes (what to capture for full PIR):
- Attach exact traces, full allocator logs, node provisioning logs, and the autoscale controller decision trace.
- Interview oncall responders to capture decision rationale and timings.
- Timeline should include exact config changes with git SHAs for knobs touched.

Open question list (for follow-up discovery):
- Did any tenant use unusually large context lengths (> 128k tokens) that could have amplified KV pressure?
- Are there other pools with the same PR rollouts that have seen smaller signs we missed?
- Can we introduce a lightweight predictive signal that alerts when kv_cache_hit_rate begins a sustained decline over 3 minutes?

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- The experimental eviction pause was useful conceptually but dangerous in practice. We need a safer atomic operation (pause + rate limiter) instead of a blunt pause.
- Consider adding a per-tenant budget for KV cache to prevent single tenant from flushing useful prefixes from global caches.

Appendix: Useful queries and links (copy-paste):
- Prometheus: rate(allocator_throttle_total[5m]) > 1 -> alert filter.
- KV cache heatmap dashboard link: internal-dashboard://kv-cache/heatmap/dedicated-prod-us-west-3-a
- Autoscale controller logs: s3://prod-logs/autoscale/controller/2025-11-08/
- Recorder trace link: trace://recorder/trace-2025-11-08-22-10

If you're reading this after a future incident: please add your notes to the bottom and ping the list above. This doc should live in the runbook index after 2 successful incident stabilizations.
